summary.text: The five regions chaotic war is the later great era in Fang Yuan's previous life, when regional order broke down, dream realms spread, and many bottom-rank Gu Masters rose.

claims.text: Fang Yuan names Hong Yi as a rank seven legend who appeared during the five regions chaotic war, with exemplary talent in self-creating killer moves and many fortuitous encounters.

In his previous life, Fang Yuan rose to become the lord of an area not only because of a blood path fortuitous encounter, but also because of the five regions chaotic war. Super forces had much lower control, and because they were focused on exploring dream realms they could not pay attention to the real world situation, which gave him time and freedom to develop. Blood path Gu Masters were hunted in ordinary times; only during the five regions chaotic war, when law and order broke down, could blood path emerge and prosper.

Toward the second half of the five regions chaotic war in that previous life, dream realms manifested on a large scale across the five regions, and dream realms becoming tribulations became more frequent, harming countless Gu Immortals. Realistically, fighting was only a small portion of a Gu Immortal’s life; only with the five regions chaotic war would fighting become the general focus.

The manifestation of dream realms gave fortuitous encounters. During the five regions chaotic war, large numbers of Gu Masters at the bottom of the hierarchy were given a chance to rise up. All sorts of people emerged, numerous like the stars in the sky. The ten great ancient sects gradually lost control, and many forces rose, including ten outstanding ones who called themselves the ten new great sects and opposed the ten ancient sects openly.

During the five regions chaotic war in Fang Yuan’s previous life, battle raged everywhere fiercely, forming an extraordinary era where countless champions emerged from the lower levels. Other than the war and the turbulence in social order, dream realms were one of the main causes of that era.
